ideas.title: Chunk the exec-side trie flush and save_books batches so consensus-thread block-tree writes stop queueing behind a 175 ms memtable insert
ideas.area: torus-state backend.rs flush (exec_pipeline.rs) / RocksDB write queue shared with hotstuff_rs block tree
ideas.what_needs_to_be_done: backend.rs:943-959 builds ONE WriteBatch (trie puts + native mirror + META_NATIVE_APPLIED_HEIGHT marker) and calls target.write(batch) once; exec_pipeline.rs:387-395 does the same for save_books. Split them into bounded chunks (start at 256 KB, env-tunable) using the chunked-writer pattern that already exists for the trade-history writer (bg_writer.rs:292-316, `chunk_kvs` policy): write trie/mirror rows in chunks, keep the applied-height marker in the LAST chunk so a crash before it replays the block (re-writes identical keys; the marker is what prevents double-apply, T156-F1). Same for save_books. Gate: land planned item A's `torus_vote_state_write_seconds` first (the uncommitted diff in the worktree adds it) and only proceed if its load-window mean is >= 5 ms with p50 < 1 ms. Validate with 3+3 interleaved cells on view_vote_delay, view_insert_persist, commit_persist_write and matched/s; also watch exec_state_write_db (total should not grow more than ~10%).
ideas.reasoning: Every block-tree write goes through RocksKVStore::write (kv_store.rs:127-146) on the DB that exec flushes into. RocksDB writers are serialized (write_other 859 vs write_self 249,536 in s65-votefix-ctl-r1 val0, so groups almost never form) and, in pipelined mode, memtable write groups run strictly one after another (JoinBatchGroup / EnterAsMemTableWriter). The exec flush is 64.39 s / 367 = 175 ms per batch (4.26 MB; buckets: 204 of 367 in 128-256 ms, 38 in 256-512, 5 in 512-1024, 1 in 1-2 s), save_books 25.36 s / 367 = 69 ms. Duty: 64.4/300 = 21% and 8.5%. Mean residual for an arrival inside an exec batch = E[L^2]/(2E[L]) ~= 0.051/(0.35) ~= 146 ms, so expected wait per independent write burst ~= 0.21 x 146 + 0.085 x 50 ~= 35 ms. Consensus-side evidence: the header handler between the ReceiveProposalHeader stamp (implementation.rs:1887) and the vote (:2043) does 3 ed25519 verifies, a handful of KV gets, one signature and two back-to-back writes (update_locks_only :2010, set_vote_state_atomic :2043); idle it takes < 1 ms (metrics-before val0: 207/220 <= 1 ms, all <= 2 ms), under load 52.1/50.6/39.7 ms (votefix-ctl-r1 val0/1/2), 48.8 (ctl-r2), 50.5/51.6/37.9 (ctl-r3), 49.7/49.5/66.4 (zerocode-ctl-r2), 36/44/36 (zerocode-ctl-r3). A follower has ~4-6 independent write bursts per view (AdvanceView #1 + enter_view, header lock+vote, AdvanceView #2, body insert/update/feed, and as next leader NewView x2 and QC collection), so the model puts 140-210 ms of the ~620 ms load-window view in write-queue waits. Chunking at 256 KB caps the memtable hold per chunk at ~175 x 0.256/4.26 ~= 10.5 ms (residual ~5 ms), so E[wait] per burst drops to ~0.21 x 5 + 0.085 x 3 ~= 1.3 ms. Upper bound ~5 x 33 = 165 ms/view; discount 50% for burst/exec timing correlation and for the share that is scheduler wake-up latency rather than queueing -> ~80 ms/view, -13% view time, ~+15% blk/s, then the +25% early-window exec cap and 0.6x dilution -> +6-10% matched/s; reported as +4-10%.

ideas.title: Skip the no-op block-tree writes: empty batches from duplicate AdvanceViews, known NewView PCs and lock-only updates still hit RocksDB
ideas.area: hotstuff_rs block_tree/accessors/internal.rs update / update_locks_only / advance_highest_pc_from_remote; pacemaker on_receive_advance_view
ideas.what_needs_to_be_done: 1) Give BlockTreeWriteBatch a dirty flag (or `is_empty()` on the WriteBatch trait; RocksWriteBatch can expose `ops.is_empty()`), and make BlockTreeSingleton::write skip `self.0.write(wb)` when nothing was set/deleted. 2) In advance_highest_pc_from_remote (internal.rs:578-617) return early when `pc.view <= highest_pc.view && !pc.phase.is_decide()` instead of writing an empty batch at :591. 3) In pacemaker on_receive_advance_view (:453-541) check `pc.view <= block_tree.highest_pc()?.view` BEFORE `pc.is_correct(block_tree)` (:475) so the re-broadcast copy (every non-collector validator re-broadcasts once, :508-527, so each node gets 2 per view) costs neither 3 ed25519 verifies nor a write. 4) In on_receive_new_view (:1537-1547) skip `update()` when the NewView's highest_pc.view <= our highest_pc.view (the next leader receives 2 NewViews per view carrying the PC it already has). Add a counter `torus_block_tree_writes_total{kind=set|empty}` to prove the count drops.
ideas.reasoning: RocksDB's WriteImpl has no empty-batch early return (db_impl_write.cc:376-384 only rejects nullptr; :984 JoinBatchGroup links every writer), so an empty batch still joins the serialized write queue and, whenever it must wait, sleeps on a futex and pays a scheduler wake-up under a 41-48 run queue. Per view per node the no-op writes are: AdvanceView #2 (advance_highest_pc_from_remote writes unconditionally at :591), NewView x2 as next leader (update() at :363 writes unconditionally; highest/lock already set, commit only ~2/3 of views), and the body-arrival update() in the ~1/3 of views without a commit (:363, inside the insert burst so cheaper). That is 2-4 avoidable write calls per view, 2-3 of them in their own burst. With the per-burst cost measured indirectly at 15-35 ms in the load window (idea 1 evidence: 2 writes + <2 ms compute = 40-52 ms vote_delay; even the blown cell s65-zerocode-ctl-r1, with exec nearly idle, showed 55 ms, so part of the cost is futex wake-up latency that any blocking write pays) the saving is ~2.5 bursts x 15-25 ms ~= 30-60 ms of a ~620 ms view = -5-9% view time, ~+5-9% blk/s, x0.6 dilution and the exec cap -> +2-4% matched/s. Also removes 3 wasted ed25519 verifies per duplicate AdvanceView (~0.2 ms CPU).

ideas.title: One durable batch before the vote (lock + vote state) and fold the B2/B3/feed bookkeeping writes into the primary batch or drop them while B3 is off
ideas.area: hotstuff_rs block_tree/accessors/internal.rs (update, update_locks_only, set_vote_state_atomic, record_leader_success, speculative commits, app-fed frontier) and hotstuff/implementation.rs header/body paths
ideas.what_needs_to_be_done: a) Header path: make update_locks_only return its BlockTreeWriteBatch (or accept `Option<(view, block)>` vote state) so implementation.rs:2010 + :2043 become ONE write containing highest_pc, locked_pc, HIGHEST_VIEW_PHASE_VOTED and LAST_VOTED_PROPOSAL; same for the full-proposal path (:1158 update + :1205 set_vote_state_atomic + :1221 set_local_tip). b) Commit burst: `update()` currently does the main write (:363) then up to 1 reputation write per QC advance (:370-381), per committed block a promote_speculative write (:387) and a reputation write (:417), and the feed then writes APP_FED_BLOCK_HEIGHT (committed_feed.rs:144). Put the reputation and speculative updates into the same batch as the commit, and defer the app-fed frontier into the next primary batch (the feed contract is at-least-once, committed_feed.rs:41-47, so a lagging frontier only re-delivers). c) While `reputation_leader_selection` is false (torus-node main.rs:318 default, :754; pacemaker :1139 returns plain IWRR), skip persisting LeaderReputation altogether (keep the in-memory cache; persist only when the switch is on) — record_leader_timeout (pacemaker :375) too. d) QC collection: advance_highest_pc_from_remote (:1468) + update (:1471) + add_speculative_commit (:1486) -> one batch. Net: ~9-13 writes per view -> ~4-5.
ideas.reasoning: Writes inside one burst are back-to-back, so they mostly share one long queue wait, but each still pays its own write-thread handoff, WAL append syscall and a possible futex sleep/wake (~0.1-1 ms uncontended, several ms when the thread loses the CPU on wake under the 41-48 run queue; the Aug-21 doc measured 20-25 ms for the leader's 6-9 writes at cap 25, size-independent). Removing 5-8 writes per view at 1-5 ms each = 5-40 ms of a ~620 ms view (-1-6%), ~+1-5% blk/s, x0.6 dilution -> +0.5-2.5% matched/s. The header-path merge additionally shortens the critical vote path that planned item A is measuring: item A makes ONE write fast, but the lock write immediately before it (:2010) has the same exposure, so without the merge vote_delay keeps one full write wait. Safety is preserved: the lock and the vote state become durable in the same atomic batch before the vote leaves (stronger than today's two-step ordering).

ideas.title: Write-through in-memory cache for the hot block-tree singletons (validator_set_state, highest_pc, locked_pc, highest_committed, highest_view_voted, highest_tc, local_tip) and a cheap contains()
ideas.area: hotstuff_rs block_tree/accessors/internal.rs + pluggables.rs (KVGet), pacemaker tick, PhaseCertificate::is_correct
ideas.what_needs_to_be_done: Extend the S395 pattern already used for LeaderReputation (internal.rs:2001-2027) and SPECULATIVE_COMMITS (:1717-1756): add RefCell<Option<..>> fields for ValidatorSetState, highest_pc, locked_pc, highest_committed_block(+height), highest_view_phase_voted, highest_tc and local_tip, populated on first read and refreshed by every setter in BlockTreeWriteBatch (the singletons are only written through BlockTreeSingleton::write, so invalidate/refresh in `write` by scanning the batch keys, or simpler: the setters record the new value on the batch and `write` applies it to the cache). Replace `contains()` (internal.rs:1056-1058, which calls `block()` = 5 KV gets incl. the ~7-13 KB compact datum, pluggables.rs:37-65) with `block_height(block).is_some()`. Optionally memoise verified PCs by (view, block, phase) so the same QC is not re-verified as AdvanceView x2, header justify, NewView x2 and body justify.
ideas.reasoning: validator_set_state() (pluggables.rs:421-428) is 4 KV gets + borsh + ValidatorSet::try_from, which does VerifyingKey::from_bytes (ed25519 point decompression, ~5-10 us) for 3 validators twice (committed + previous, validator_set.rs:192-219) ~= 50-80 us per call. It is called once per algorithm-loop iteration by pacemaker.tick (:100) plus 16 sites in hotstuff/implementation.rs and 4 in the pacemaker; the loop iterates once per message or every 10 ms while fetches are pending (algorithm.rs:283-296), i.e. ~15-25 iterations per loaded view (val0.log.gz has 8,139 hotstuff on_receive_msg lines over ~1,441 views, plus pacemaker messages and timeouts). ~30-40 calls x 60 us ~= 2-2.5 ms; highest_pc() is read 2-3x per tick (:194-201) ~60 x 5 us = 0.3 ms; contains() 6-10 x ~30 us = 0.3 ms; redundant QC verifies 6-9 x 55 us = 0.4 ms. Total ~3-4 ms per view of the consensus thread's ~102-110 ms on-CPU per view (summary.json consensus_thread_ms_per_view_est), i.e. 3-4% of its CPU; with ~0.6 ms of run-queue wait per on-CPU ms (90-105 ms runqueue per 162 ms on-CPU, s64 #9) that is ~5-6 ms wall per 620 ms view ~= 1% -> +0.5-1.5% matched/s. Below the 9-10% MDE on its own; bundle with ideas 2-3.

1) Evidence that changes an existing estimate: the s64 §3 item 'consensus KV split instance (ebcfc46, n=1, exec-bound era; re-test only if item 9 implicates the write queue)' — the arithmetic here implicates it. In s65-votefix-ctl-r1 val0 the exec flush holds the serialized RocksDB write path 21% of the load window in 175 ms (mean; tail to 1-2 s) single batches, save_books another 8.5% in 69 ms batches, and write groups almost never form (write_other 859 vs write_self 249,536). Expected wait for a random consensus-thread write burst ~= 0.21 x 146 ms (length-biased residual, E[L^2]/2E[L]) + 0.085 x 50 ~= 35 ms. The header handler (implementation.rs:1887 -> :2043: 3 verifies, a few gets, 1 sign, 2 back-to-back writes) takes < 1 ms idle (metrics-before: 207/220 <= 1 ms) and 36-66 ms in the load window in every s65 cell. With 4-6 independent write bursts per view that is ~140-210 ms of the ~620 ms view, a candidate for much of the 70% futex_wait_queue time (RocksDB WriteThread::AwaitState blocks on a condvar). The split-instance re-test deserves the same priority as idea 1 above; it preserves exec-batch atomicity where chunking does not.
2) Caveat on the model: s65-zerocode-ctl-r1 is a blown cell (5,011 matched/s, 2.4 s views, only 61 exec batches) and still shows vote_delay 55/57/28 ms with exec nearly idle, so part of the per-write cost is likely scheduler wake-up latency after the futex sleep (run queue 41-48 on 18 cores), not queueing alone. Both causes are reduced by fewer blocking writes (ideas 2-3); only the queueing part is reduced by idea 1. The uncommitted worktree diff (kv_store.rs with_metrics -> torus_vote_state_write_seconds, 10 us buckets) is the direct test: prediction if queueing dominates: load-window mean 15-25 ms, p50 < 1 ms, tail to 0.5-1 s tracking exec_state_write_db's tail; if it reads < 2 ms mean, drop idea 1 and keep ideas 2-4. Note that item A instruments only the batch carrying HIGHEST_VIEW_PHASE_VOTED; the lock write at :2010 immediately before it is not timed, so add a second histogram for it (or time every BlockTreeSingleton::write by key class) in the same change.
3) If the s65-zerocode control mean includes ctl-r1 it is biased low (5k vs 57-67k in r2/r3); check how the campaign summary averaged the ctl arm before drawing conclusions from the push/r270 comparisons.
4) Possible bugs / waste found (not counted as ideas): (a) pacemaker on_receive_advance_view verifies the PC's 3 signatures (:475) and writes (:488 -> internal.rs:591) before discovering it is stale — every node processes 2 AdvanceViews per view because of the re-broadcast at :508-527; (b) record_leader_success/timeout persist LeaderReputation on every QC advance, commit and timeout even though reputation_leader_selection defaults to false (main.rs:318) and select_leader_with_reputation ignores it (pacemaker :1139); (c) BlockTreeWriteBatch setters mislabel errors as Key::HighestTC for LOCAL_TIP, LAST_VOTED_PROPOSAL, SPECULATIVE_COMMITS, LEADER_REPUTATION, HIGHEST_VIEW_ENTERED and HIGHEST_PC (cosmetic, but misleading in logs); (d) highest_view_voted is read twice back-to-back at :1178-1179, :1334-1335, :2018-2019.
5) What is NOT a problem in this angle: the block datum is the compact encoding (~7-13 KB for 200 hashes, app.rs:4714-4730, COMPACT_PROPOSALS=true at :2553), so block-tree reads are small; disk wait is < 0.5% and cf_consensus_meta has an 8 MiB memtable with bloom filters (db.rs:265-302), so KV gets are memtable/block-cache hits. The read side is a CPU item (idea 4), not a latency item.
6) Devnet runs with --retention-blocks 100000 (test_harness.py:393), so the pruner's per-commit pass (internal.rs:1834-1894) is effectively idle during a 300 s cell (never reaches the horizon).

ideas.title: Break the pacemaker's period-2 limit cycle: the absolute deadline grid never rebases when the fleet is slower than max_view_time, so every other view is burned instantly
ideas.area: hotstuff_rs pacemaker (update_view / update_timeouts), genesis timeout_base_ms
ideas.what_needs_to_be_done: Mechanism (crates/hotstuff_rs/src/pacemaker/implementation.rs): view deadlines come from an absolute per-epoch grid `epoch_start_time + max_view_time*k` (update_timeouts :894-901). update_view rebases the grid ONLY when the replica is >2x AHEAD of it (:610-613); a backed-off entry rewrites only that one view's slot (:623-633). Under load the fleet's certificate-to-certificate round is ~650-840 ms (> the 500 ms slot), so after the first backed-off (1 s) view succeeds, the next certificate-driven entry has stall multiplier 1 and a grid deadline already in the past -> tick() times it out on the next loop iteration (:103), broadcasts a TimeoutVote, and with f=0 at n=3 the Bracha rule (:307-318, accumulated_power > f where f=(3-1)/3=0) makes the other two abandon the view too -> TC -> the following view gets multiplier 2 (1 s) and succeeds -> repeat. Result: [instant-burn view][productive 1 s view] forever. Fix, two parts: (1) give certificate-driven entries a deadline that fits the loaded round: either genesis `timeout_base_ms` 500 -> ~1200 (no code; every 500 ms slot then exceeds the round, the fleet runs AHEAD of the grid and the existing S395 rebase keeps it synced), or an adaptive base `max(base, 1.5 * EWMA(last 8 certificate-to-certificate intervals))` clamped to 4*base; (2) make the rebase symmetric: in update_view, when `next_view == highest_qc_view + 1` (healthy entry) and `scheduled < now + max_view_time`, call `update_timeouts(next_view, ...)` so the entered view gets a full slot from now. Add a unit test next to the S395 tests (:1460-1510): a replica whose rounds take 1.3x max_view_time must not time out any certificate-driven view. Validate with the timeout telemetry (idea 3) and `views_per_committed_block` in the load window; the crash cell (--crash-at 60) guards recovery time.
ideas.reasoning: Every timed-out view in the healthy cells is one where an honest leader was mid-work or where the grid burned the view instantly; nobody is dead. Deadlines are free when progress happens (a view ends on the AdvanceView/PC, :529-537, not on the deadline), so a bigger slot costs nothing in the healthy case; the only cost is dead-leader recovery, which at n=3 is moot (the chain halts with one node down anyway) and at n=4 is <=1 s per dead-leader view. Arithmetic: ctl-r2 load window val0 = 586 views for 403 committed blocks (1.454 views/block), 156 timeouts. Fleet-wide, 558 produce_block calls but only 451 distinct parents: 107 doomed builds in 88 re-propose runs, and the wall time spent inside those runs (first doomed produce -> the produce that finally survived) is 44.4 s of the 300 s window (14.8%). s55 measured views/block 1.50 -> 1.07 at base 1500 ms (cap 100, exec-bound, so no throughput signal then). Removing ~75% of the re-propose dead time frees ~33 s/300 s -> +11-13% blk/s in the consensus-bound early window; after the 0.6x late-window dilution used in the s64 report that is +6-9% matched/s; I report +5-10%.

ideas.title: Budget-aware proposing: a leader that enters its view with less budget than build+finalize+vote must not build (and push) a 200-action block that is doomed
ideas.area: hotstuff_rs enter_view proposer arm + torus-consensus app.rs produce_block (payload selector)
ideas.what_needs_to_be_done: S variant (hotstuff_rs only): in `enter_view`'s `Phase::Generic | Phase::Decide` arm (crates/hotstuff_rs/src/hotstuff/implementation.rs ~:585, before `app.produce_block`) compute `remaining = self.view_info.deadline.saturating_duration_since(Instant::now())`; if `remaining < MIN_PROPOSE_BUDGET` (finalize ~100 ms + header arrival ~15 + vote ~50 + QC ~30 + a 50 ms margin ≈ 250 ms, env-tunable `TORUS_MIN_PROPOSE_BUDGET_MS`), skip the build for this view (log + counter `torus_proposals_skipped_no_budget_total`) so the thread is free to process the next view's header. Re-check the deadline again after `produce_block` returns and before `broadcast_proposal_as_header` (:~717) so a block that took too long is not pushed as 2x ~3.6 MB pre-proposal bodies. M variant: add `deadline: Instant` to `ProduceBlockRequest` (crates/hotstuff_rs/src/app.rs:252-270, plus a pub getter) and in app.rs produce_block (:4424; cap applied at :5113/:5147 via `native_total_block_cap()`) scale the native cap to what fits: `cap = min(200, (remaining - 250 ms) / 1.35 ms)` (273 ms build / 200 actions from `view_propose_build_ms`). Keep the vote/insert paths untouched; this is proposer-local and cannot fork.
ideas.reasoning: In ctl-r2 15% of leaders (18 of 124 in the 2-min slice) start produce_block more than 500 ms after the QC that made them leader, i.e. already past a multiplier-1 deadline; each then spends ~273 ms building + ~96 ms finalizing + pushes ~7 MB of body to peers, and both followers spend ~40-170 ms validating a block that no one can vote on. Fleet-wide that is 107 doomed builds x ~370 ms ≈ 40 s of consensus-thread time per 300 s (≈13 s per node, 4.4% of the thread's wall) plus ~770 MB of wasted pushes and ~200 wasted follower validates. The thread time matters because it is on the critical path: while val1 built its stale 786 block (04.538-04.58 + finalize) it could not process val0's 787 header until 04.902, which killed 787 as well (cascade 786->787->788, 3.4 s). The 16 runs of >=3 doomed builds account for ~12 s of the 44.4 s of re-propose dead time; converting doomed views into either an early hand-off (S) or a smaller block that survives (M) recovers a share of that. Estimate: S variant recovers ~1/3 of the cascade time (~4-6 s/300 s -> +2-3% blk/s early window -> +1-2% matched/s) and cuts leader CPU; M variant additionally commits partial blocks in short-budget views: +3-5% blk/s early -> +2-3% matched/s. raw.notes:
Surprises and evidence that change existing estimates:
1. Timeouts are NOT rare glitches: in the ctl-r2 load window the fleet built 558 blocks to commit ~403; 107 builds were doomed re-proposals of the same parent, and 44.4 s of the 300 s window (14.8%) elapsed inside re-propose runs. This is the single largest identifiable consensus-side waste I found, larger than any per-view timer item in the s64 top 10, and it is invariant across every s65 arm (timeouts 116-168, views/block 1.38-1.55 in 11 cells), so none of the s65 A/Bs touched it.
2. The s55 'raise timeout_base_ms: null result' verdict should be retired. Deadlines are free on the happy path (views end on the certificate, pacemaker :529-537), the s55 cell was exec-bound at cap 100 with 40% noise, and views/block did move 1.50 -> 1.07 there. A genesis-only 500 -> 1200 ms A/B at cap 200 is the cheapest experiment on the table; the code-level version (symmetric grid rebase + adaptive slot) is idea 1.
3. Possible bug / design flaw: update_view's rebase is one-sided (:610). The S395 comment (:582-591) says a replica BEHIND the grid 'burns through missed views instantly' as if that were harmless; under sustained load it makes the replica emit TimeoutVotes for views the fleet is actively working on, and with f=0 Bracha (:307-318) one such vote ends the view for everyone. Grid phases also differ per node (rebased at different instants): val2 timed out view 786 at ~13504.03, ~250 ms after the fleet entered it (~13503.78), while val0 timed it out at ~13504.33.
4. Simultaneous consensus-thread silence: around 13501.4-13503.5 all three hotstuff-algo threads logged nothing for 1.4-2.1 s (val1 right after 'validate_block called' for height 684; val0 after serving a body fetch; val2 after its commit feed). recv_timeout would have returned at the deadline (receiving.rs:177-178), and the local view did not advance, so the threads were blocked inside a handler, not waiting for messages. Per node the >0.9 s gaps sum to 26-43 s per 300 s (9-14% of wall). This is consistent with the planned item A (vote-state persist) or the commit-feed write contending with the exec thread's 300+ ms flushes on the shared RocksDB; the wchan sampler cannot separate a channel wait from a lock wait (7004 futex vs 2918 running samples for the three tids). Worth checking the A-vs-ctl cells for these gaps specifically (the awk over 'on_receive_msg|validate_block called|produce_block called|on_committed_block' timestamps is cheap).
5. Repeated validation: val0/val1/val2 called validate_block 375/359/374 times for 339/319/329 distinct heights in the load window (34-43 heights validated 2-3 times, e.g. height 686 at 08.289, 08.470, 08.504 on val2). Each is 40-170 ms on the consensus thread; probably the header-path + body-path + missing-data retry combination (algorithm.rs tick_missing_data_retries). Not my angle, but a cheap dedup.
6. 58 produce_block calls in the load window have no matching 'selected actions for block' line (558 vs 500). Either the selector took a different log path or those builds were abandoned/empty; whoever implements idea 2 should check produce_block :4424-4626 for the early-return paths before trusting the 107 doomed-build count (it can only be higher).
7. Late-vote loss at the next leader is small: val0 saw 155 views with 3 PhaseVotes, 9 with 2, 5 with 1 (8% partial). Keeping the previous view's vote collector alive after a view change (types.rs:345 drops votes whose view != collector view) would rescue at most those; not worth a separate item.
8. The pre-proposal FULL-BODY push (~3.6 MB to each peer per build, log-summary.json body_push 170-185 per node) is also spent on every doomed build (~770 MB per 300 s fleet-wide); the s64 hash-only-push item gets a bit stronger from that.

ideas.title: Progress-relative view deadlines: stop orphaning 1 in 5 proposals to the earliest node's absolute timer
ideas.area: hotstuff_rs pacemaker (view schedule) + timeout amplification
ideas.what_needs_to_be_done: In crates/hotstuff_rs/src/pacemaker/implementation.rs, make the deadline of an entered view relative to its entry instant instead of a slot in a per-node absolute table: in update_view (:556-658) set timeouts[next_view] = Instant::now() + max_view_time * stall_multiplier(...) unconditionally (today it reads the absolute schedule built by initial_timeouts :838-841 / update_timeouts :894-900, whose base is each node's own Instant::now() at boot or at every rebase :830/:885, so the three nodes' deadlines for the same view differ by up to one slot). Keep the Task A / S470 multiplier (so genuine stalls still back off), keep extend_epoch_change_view_timeout, and keep the S395 far-future clamp (:610-613) as a no-op guard. Update the stateright lockstep tests (tests/stateright_lockstep_backoff.rs) and the schedule tests at :1441-1904. Validation first (no code): in devnet/genesis.json set timeout_base_ms 1000 and 1500 (3+3 cells vs control at cap 200) and score the NEW metric orphaned_proposals = sum(view_propose_delay_count) - sum(view_qc_collect_count) over the load window (475 - 376 = 99 in s65-votefix-ctl-r1); it must go to ~0 and blk/s must rise. Then implement the relative timer so failure detection stays at 500 ms instead of 1.5 s.
ideas.reasoning: Views advance in two ways: a QC (AdvanceView) or a purely local timer (tick :174-179 calls update_view(cur+1) with no TC). Each node's timer for view v is an absolute instant in its own table, so the fleet's effective deadline for v is min over the three nodes; when the first node leaves v it drops every HotStuff message for v (receiving.rs:268-272 requires view == cur_view; header vote gate header_is_current :1890) and its TimeoutVote alone (2,000,000 > f = 1,999,999, :303-318) drags the others out. Because the quorum at n=3 is 3/3, one early exit orphans the whole proposal. Loaded views take 632 ms (307.6 s / 487) against a 500 ms slot, so this happens constantly. Arithmetic (s65-votefix-ctl-r1 load window): 556 views, 475 proposals, 376 certified, 375 committed -> 99 orphaned proposals (20.8%). Each orphan ran to the earliest deadline, ~0.55 s (consecutive-view median 521 ms) -> 99 x 0.55 = 54 s of the 307 s window produced no block. Removing them: 375 blocks / (307 - 54) s x 307 s = 455 blocks, i.e. blk/s up to +21%. The 103 dead views cost ~0 wall time (they are skipped on the next tick; val0's log shows no message ever delivered in them) so only commit latency improves from those. Applying the s64 dilution rule (0.6x, early-window exec cap +25%): +8-13% matched/s upper, so +5-12%. Timeouts 127-140 per node (23-25% of views) should fall below 5%, commit_interval p95 3.5 s should roughly halve because the 2-chain rule (block_tree/invariants.rs:617) stops being broken by dead views.

memory a0a6940c337429bc (S395: quorum is all 3, f=0) and e2529a8ef114b884 (schedule is linear cumulative per-epoch)
docs/perf/blown-cell-diagnosis-2026-09-17.md section 2 (timeout cliff 19-29%, views/block 1.6) and section 4 (s55 timeout A/B null at cap 100, +/-40% noise)

Neither identifies that 21% of loaded proposals are orphaned, nor the mechanism (three unsynchronized absolute schedules + f+1 = one validator amplification + past-view message drop), nor that dead views themselves cost no wall time. ideas.title: Vote lane at the next leader: dispatch queued PhaseVotes ahead of the 4 MB body so the QC forms ~240 ms earlier
ideas.area: hotstuff_rs algorithm loop / progress-message receive ordering
ideas.what_needs_to_be_done: Votes for view v go only to leader(v+1) (roles.rs:219-236), which is also the node that must fetch, validate and insert B_v's body before it can propose (implementation.rs:593-605). Both the PhaseVotes and the BlockDataResponse arrive on the same FIFO and the loop handles one message per iteration (algorithm.rs:297-334; BlockDataResponse dispatch implementation.rs:975-977 -> on_receive_block_data_response :2210 -> try_insert_body :2385, which runs validate_block, the insert and the commit feed inline). Change: in ProgressMessageStub::recv (networking/receiving.rs:162-190) or in the loop, drain any PhaseVote/AdvanceView messages for the current view before dispatching a BlockDataResponse (a two-lane dequeue: small consensus messages first, bodies second). Optionally, when the QC for v forms before the body is inserted, mark the parent as pending so enter_view does not issue a second request_missing_parent (:2852) for a body already in flight.
ideas.reasoning: qc_collect at the proposer is 303 ms (36.68 s / 121) although vote_delay is 52 ms and header delivery is ~14 ms: the remaining ~240 ms equals the collector's body work (insert_persist 179 ms measured from header arrival, plus the ~120-150 ms commit feed that update() runs inside try_insert_body). So the QC for B_v is assembled only after leader(v+1) has finished follower duty for B_v. Forming the QC at ~70 ms instead of ~300 ms after the header does not shorten the view directly (the leader still needs the parent inserted to build), but it certifies the block ~230 ms before the earliest node's deadline can strike, converting orphaned proposals (idea 1) into harmless dead views, and it sends the AdvanceView to the other two nodes earlier. Arithmetic: today the QC lands ~392 + 303 = ~695 ms after view start while the effective slot is <= 500 ms + schedule skew; moving the QC to ~460 ms puts most of the 99 orphans inside the slot. If half of them are saved: 50 x 0.55 s = 27 s of 307 s -> +10% blk/s; after the 0.6x dilution +3-6% matched/s. With idea 1 in place the gain shrinks to the earlier AdvanceView alone (~1-2%).
evidence: sampler.csv load-window val0: qc_collect 36.68 s/121 = 303 ms; vote_delay 15.46 s/297 = 52 ms; insert_persist 33.11 s/185 = 179 ms; propose_delay 61.23 s/156 = 392 ms

networking/receiving.rs:162-190 (FIFO, current-view buffer first, no priority by message type)

hotstuff/implementation.rs:593-605 (proposer defers until the parent body is in the tree), roles.rs:219-236 (votes go to leader(v+1))

ideas.expected_improvement: +3-6% matched/s standalone (orphans roughly halved); ~+1-2% once idea 1 lands
ideas.risk: Reordering within a view is safety-neutral (votes need no body; safe_pc still gates the QC :1455-1462), but starving body dispatch behind a vote flood is impossible at n=3 and must be bounded at n>=4 (drain at most n votes). The magnitude depends on the body-vs-vote arrival race, which I inferred from averages, not per-view traces; TORUS_BODY_FETCH_TRACE=1 cells can confirm the order.

It does not identify that the next leader's vote collection is serialized behind the body insert and feed in the shared FIFO, which is what sets qc_collect at 303 ms, nor that earlier certification protects the block from the timeout cut-off.

ideas.title: Leader tenure of 2-4 views: keep the proposer that already holds the parent and an idle thread
ideas.area: hotstuff_rs leader selection (select_leader) + genesis parameter
ideas.what_needs_to_be_done: Add a fleet-uniform leader_tenure (genesis field, default 1 = today) and select the leader with select_leader(view / tenure) in pacemaker/implementation.rs:1040 (all routing already goes through select_leader / select_leader_with_reputation: roles.rs:74-140, 219-275, implementation.rs:1709-1714, 2819, block_tree internal.rs:378/540). Memory de0d28debfb5e166 records that exactly this plumbing existed in May 2026 (S254 stable-leader, tenure=100, threaded through ChainConfig/PacemakerConfiguration) and was dropped with the CTE rewrite; the git history of this line does not contain it, so it must be re-done. Pairs naturally with the never-implemented speculative pre-build (docs/plans/speculative-pipelining-impl.md Task C4 'predict next proposer' becomes trivial for views 2..k of a tenure).
ideas.reasoning: With equal stakes IWRR rotates the leader every view (index = view % total_power, pos_in_row = index % 3). The cost of that rotation is that leader(v+1) is the one node whose follower work for B_v is on the critical path: it must wait for the body (header->body 45-52 ms avg, p90 120), reconstruct/attest it (~60 ms), insert it (insert_persist 179 ms end-to-end) and run the commit feed before it can build, and its queued votes wait behind that work (qc_collect 303 ms). Estimated per-view critical path: build 185 + own insert ~70 + feed ~135 + QC ~80 = ~470 ms vs 632 ms measured (-25%). Tenure 2: (632+470)/2 = 551 ms (-13%); tenure 4: (632+3x470)/4 = 511 ms (-19%); blk/s +15% / +24% upper bound. After the s64 dilution (0.6x, early exec cap) that is +6-10% (k=2) and +8-14% (k=4). Shorter views also reduce the orphan rate of idea 1.

raw.notes:
1) The '~1.5 views per committed block' decomposes, in the s65-votefix-ctl-r1 load window, into 375 committed blocks + 103 dead views (entered and left with no message; ~0 wall time; uniform over leader slots 35/35/33) + 99 orphaned proposals (built, broadcast, voted, never certified; ~0.55 s each). Only the orphans cost throughput; the dead views cost commit latency via the consecutive-view rule (invariants.rs:617). This changes the s64 reading of the timeout knob: it is not a null lever, the s55 A/B (cap 100, +/-40% noise) could not have seen a +20% blk/s effect, and the right score is sum(propose_delay_count) - sum(qc_collect_count), which the harness can compute from sampler.csv today.
2) Possible bug: the pacemaker's 'lockstep by construction' comments (implementation.rs:620-622, 773-778) assume identical schedules, but the schedule base is each node's local Instant::now() at boot and at every rebase (:830, :885), and rebases happen independently whenever a node runs >2 slots ahead (idle/drain at ~30 blk/s). Nodes therefore hold different absolute deadlines for the same view, and with n=3 (quorum 3/3, Bracha threshold satisfied by one validator) the earliest node's timer decides the fleet's deadline. This is also why the S470 commit-lag term can flip the multiplier on one node before the others.
3) Evidence changing an existing estimate: s64 item 1's follower-side coupling is stronger than stated. On leader(v+1) the commit feed runs inside try_insert_body before the queued votes are read, so the QC for the previous block (qc_collect 303 ms vs vote_delay 52 ms) is delayed by the feed as well; deferring the feed only on the leader's propose path leaves ~120-150 ms of it in front of the QC. The deferred-feed change should cover try_insert_body's update() too.
4) Unverified: when the QC arrives before the body, enter_view's am_proposer branch calls request_missing_parent (:2852) which is guarded only by deferred_bodies, so a second 4 MB body request may be issued while the first fetch is in flight. Worth a TORUS_BODY_FETCH_TRACE check.
5) Broadcast semantics: swarm.rs:2191-2193 enqueues every broadcast to the local inbound queue (self-delivery), while the direct fan excludes self (:2673-2685). So the QC-collecting leader enters v+1 through its own AdvanceView without a network round trip; the leader-change cost is the next leader's follower work, not vote routing.
6) Memory get_memory requires the field name 'id' (not 'memory_id').

ideas.title: One write-group join on the follower header-vote path (fold lock + leader-reputation + vote-state into a single batch)
ideas.area: hotstuff_rs header fast path / block_tree writes (crates/hotstuff_rs/src/hotstuff/implementation.rs on_receive_proposal_header ~L1871-2100; crates/hotstuff_rs/src/block_tree/accessors/internal.rs update_locks_only L499, set_leader_reputation L2030, set_vote_state_atomic L645)
ideas.what_needs_to_be_done: On the header path every follower (and the next leader, which is what matters) issues THREE separate RocksDB writes before its vote leaves: (1) update_locks_only builds a batch (highest_pc + locked_pc) and calls self.write(wb) (internal.rs ~L525); (2) inside the same function record_leader_success -> set_leader_reputation issues its OWN write (internal.rs L2030-2050, unconditional, even with B3 reputation not enabled for leader selection); (3) set_vote_state_atomic issues a third write (L645-663), now placed before the send (f05b20e, implementation.rs L2098). Each write is RocksKVStore::write -> self.db.write(batch) (torus-consensus/src/kv_store.rs L142-170) on the SAME rocksdb instance as exec/state (main.rs L569: RocksKVStore::new(state_db.db_arc())), so each call is a separate write-group join (librocksdb-sys db_impl_write.cc L552/L984: JoinBatchGroup is unconditional) that can queue behind a multi-MB exec batch. Change: add a BlockTreeSingleton::vote_on_header(justify, view, block_hash) that appends highest_pc/locked_pc, the LEADER_REPUTATION value (via the existing write-through RefCell cache) and HIGHEST_VIEW_PHASE_VOTED + LAST_VOTED_PROPOSAL into ONE BlockTreeWriteBatch, written once, then send the vote. Ordering invariants are preserved because the single atomic batch is durable before the send (lock-before-vote and persist-before-send both hold). Add a counter of consensus-meta writes per view (or reuse vote_state_write_seconds) to prove the join count dropped 3 -> 1.
ideas.reasoning: vote_delay (header arrival -> vote sent) is ~5.4 ms averaged over a whole run (s65-zerocode-ctl-r1 val0: 4.73 s / 873 = 5.4 ms) but 17-78 ms (mean ~48) in the 30 s load windows of s65-votefix-fix-r1 val0. The CPU work on that path is identical in both regimes (3 ed25519 verifies ~0.2 ms, ~10 KV gets, a borsh sign); the only load-dependent components are the three write-group joins, so each join costs roughly (48-5)/3 ~ 14 ms under load (the s65 vote-fix memory records the same mechanism: 'vote-state write joins the shared RocksDB write group behind 4 MB exec batches'). Planned item A makes the vote-state write fast, which removes at most one of the three joins; the lock batch and the reputation write stay. Folding all three into one batch removes two more joins: ~2 x 14 = ~28 ms. This path is on the next leader's critical chain (single-threaded: header -> vote -> body insert -> QC -> build), and insert_persist (111-212 ms in the load windows) contains it. 28 ms out of a 620-680 ms view = 4-4.5 % fewer ms per view; blk/s +3-5 %; matched/s scales less in the exec-bound late minutes, so +2-4 %.

ideas.title: Skip empty and no-op consensus-meta writes: empty batches still join the RocksDB write group (AdvanceView duplicates, NewView update(), leader's self-header lock write)
ideas.area: hotstuff_rs block_tree write plumbing + NewView/AdvanceView handlers (internal.rs write L202, update L330, advance_highest_pc_from_remote L578; kv_store.rs L142; implementation.rs on_receive_new_view L1568-1600; pacemaker/implementation.rs on_receive_advance_view L453-540)
ideas.what_needs_to_be_done: 1) In RocksKVStore::write (kv_store.rs L142) return early when wb.ops is empty (and likewise in BlockTreeSingleton::write). RocksDB has no empty-batch short-circuit: DBImpl::WriteImpl / PipelinedWriteImpl call JoinBatchGroup unconditionally (db_impl_write.cc L552, L984), so an empty batch waits for whatever write group is in flight. 2) In update() (internal.rs L330-364) and advance_highest_pc_from_remote (L578-600) skip the write when nothing was set. 3) In on_receive_new_view (implementation.rs L1583-1590) only run block_tree.update when new_view.highest_pc.view > highest_pc().view; otherwise the PC was already delivered by the AdvanceView (pacemaker L529-536 enters the view from it) and the NewView is pure duplicate work (3 verifies + safe_pc + a write). Optionally drop NewView entirely on the pipelined path since AdvanceView already reaches the next leader.
ideas.reasoning: Per view each node receives 2 AdvanceViews (the QC-forming leader broadcasts in tick L193-214, the other replica re-broadcasts on receipt L506-527); the second one finds highest_pc already advanced and advance_highest_pc_from_remote writes an EMPTY batch (1 join). The next leader receives 2-3 NewViews (sent unconditionally in enter_view L451-472, including to itself via the SelfDelivered path) and runs update() on each: verify 3 signatures, safe_pc, then a write that is empty or redundant (2-3 joins). The leader processes its own self-delivered header (main.rs L835 comment) through the follower path: update_locks_only writes an empty batch because its own update() already advanced highest_pc/lock (1 join), then set_vote_state_atomic (needed). That is 4-5 avoidable write-group joins per view per node; at the ~14 ms/join inferred under load (idea 1) that is up to ~60 ms of consensus-thread occupancy per view. Most of it is off the critical path, but the loop is single-threaded FIFO (algorithm.rs poll_progress_and_retry handles one message per iteration), so a join queued ahead of the next header, a vote or a pushed body delays it. Estimate: 10-30 % of that time lands on the critical chain -> 6-18 ms of a 620-680 ms view -> +1-3 % blk/s; matched/s +0.5-2 %.

ideas.area: hotstuff_rs certificate verification (hotstuff/types.rs PhaseCertificate::is_correct L48-147, is_correctly_signed L149-183; call sites implementation.rs L1958 header justify, L1583 NewView, pacemaker L475 AdvanceView, block_sync/client.rs L566/L630)

Also hoist the (chain_id, view, block, phase).try_to_vec() out of the per-signature loop in is_correctly_signed (it is re-serialized once per signature).

Average ~13-15 per node per view, ~20 on the next leader. At ~50-60 us per verify (curve25519-dalek 4.1.3, x86-64) that is 0.7-1.2 ms, plus 5 KV gets and two ValidatorSet deserializations per is_correct call (validator_set_state() rebuilds both sets from RocksDB on every call, pluggables.rs L421) ~0.3 ms. Total ~1-1.5 ms per 620-680 ms view = 0.2 %. The memo keeps one verification per distinct PC, so it saves ~70 % of that: ~1 ms/view, +0.1-0.3 %. The same PC is verified 4-6 times per view across the handlers (header, 2 AdvanceView, NewView, occasionally advertise), so the redundancy is real, just cheap.

ideas.title: Certificate-driven view entry gets a relative deadline (now + max_view_time) instead of the absolute epoch slot, plus a doomed-build guard
ideas.area: hotstuff_rs pacemaker schedule (pacemaker/implementation.rs update_view L560-660, update_timeouts L868-900, stall_multiplier L780; hotstuff/implementation.rs enter_view L349-660)
ideas.what_needs_to_be_done: In update_view, when the entry is driven by a certificate (AdvanceView PC / collected PC / TC) rather than by a local timeout, set timeouts[next_view] = max(scheduled, now + max_view_time * multiplier). Keep the absolute schedule for timeout-driven entries (it is what keeps replicas in lockstep during no-quorum churn) and keep the S395 ahead-of-schedule rebase (L610-613) and the Task A backoff (L618-635). In enter_view, before produce_block, skip building if the view's deadline is already in the past or closer than the recent block_build EWMA, and re-check the deadline after produce_block before broadcast_proposal_as_header so a header for an already-dead view is not broadcast (followers currently fetch and insert such bodies because headers bypass view filtering, implementation.rs L1876-1880).
ideas.reasoning: The schedule assigns view k the absolute deadline epoch_start + (k - s + 1) x 500 ms (update_timeouts L889-898, timeout_base_ms 500 in devnet/wsl/genesis-3val.json and main.rs L314). Load-window views take 535-780 ms (s65-votefix-fix-r1 val0 30 s windows), so every certificate-driven entry inherits a slot that is already partly or fully consumed; the drift is paid as a timed-out view roughly every 500/(view-500) real views. Measured: 12-19 timeouts per 30 s against 44-56 views (27-35 % of views) and 1.3-1.5 views per block, matching this arithmetic (drift 120-280 ms per real view -> one burned slot every 2-4 views). A burned view costs the time from entry to the deadline (0-500 ms, mean ~150-250 ms once the Task A stretch alternation is included) and, when the deadline falls inside the leader's ~320 ms build (enter_view runs produce_block before the next tick can time the view out), a doomed proposal that all three nodes still fetch and validate (~100-150 ms each on the single consensus thread). 13-19 burned views x 150-250 ms = 2-4.7 s per 30 s = 7-16 % of wall time; net of the doomed-build side effects and the fact that some burns are instant, expect +3-10 % blk/s. The s55 cap-100 A/B that raised timeout_base_ms to 1500 removed the dead views (1.5 -> 1.07 views/block, 24 % -> 3 % timeouts) and measured ms/block -20 % +/- 50 %: a +10-16 % effect is inside that noise, so the null verdict is not evidence against it at cap 200 with n=3 interleaved cells.

ideas.title: Stop pushing bodies every validator already holds: skip the pre-proposal body push when gossip is on, and dedup pushed bodies by hash before decode/mirror
ideas.area: torus-network swarm.rs / bridge.rs, torus-mempool ingest, bench env
ideas.what_needs_to_be_done: (a) Bench/env first: run an arm with TORUS_HASH_ONLY_PUSH_THRESHOLD=1 (bridge.rs:118-133 clamps any requested value <= floor, so 1 byte makes every non-empty body set hash-only; receivers then only do ~200 `contains` reads on the swarm thread, swarm.rs:2462-2466, and pull nothing because everything is present). (b) Code: add an explicit off switch (skip the PreProposalBundle send in app.rs:4693-4707 or the worker at main.rs:710-718) so neither the bodies nor the manifest are sent when native gossip is enabled. (c) For production, where gossip may lag, make the push receive path decode-free for duplicates: prefix each pushed entry with its action hash (or send hashes first) and check the pool hash_index / DA `contains` BEFORE `decode_pre_proposal_batch` (swarm.rs:1492-1510) and before `mirror_to_da`; today `add_native_action_from_gossip` mirrors first (lib.rs:482-487, 811-837) and `put_batch` has no presence check (native_da.rs:87-110), so every pushed duplicate is re-cloned, re-serialized, re-hashed, re-written to RocksDB and only then dropped by the trust-cache dedup. (d) If the push stays on: compress each fan-out envelope once. `fan_native_push` (swarm.rs:2486-2540) hands the same Arc payload to one `send_request` per peer and the codec zstd-compresses it per stream (codec.rs:265-285), i.e. N-1 identical 3.8 MB compressions per led block.
ideas.reasoning: Load-window push = 200 bodies = ~3.8 MB (val0.log.excerpt: 'pre-proposal FULL-BODY push count=200 bytes=3797303'); per node ~0.73 pushes/s received and ~0.37 led blocks/s sent. Sender per led block: 2 x zstd(3.8 MB, level 3, ~400 MB/s) ~= 19 ms + 2 borsh copies ~= 21 ms swarm-thread CPU -> ~8 ms/s. Receiver per push: decompress ~2.5 ms + borsh copy ~1 ms + bincode decode of 80k orders ~4-8 ms on the swarm thread (-> 6-9 ms/s), then on the gossip-verify pool 200 x (clone + bincode + keccak + EIP-712 cache key ~100-200 us) = 20-40 ms (-> 15-30 ms/s), plus 3.8 MB x 0.73/s ~= 2.8 MB/s of duplicate WAL+memtable bytes (~8% of the 33-36 MB/s WAL) and a proportional share of the 0.65 core/node compaction CPU (~0.05 core). Total ~0.1-0.15 core per node, 0.3-0.45 core host-wide, plus fewer memtable flushes. The HotStuff thread is untouched, so the gain is CPU relief on a shared 18-core host: 0-2% matched/s, most likely near 0 on this bench, but it is free and it removes ~1.2 GB of duplicate RocksDB writes per node per cell.

ideas.title: One-hop consensus delivery: let the swarm thread hand messages straight to the algo thread's channel and remove the poller thread's 250 us park
ideas.area: hotstuff_rs networking/receiving.rs + torus-network bridge.rs
ideas.what_needs_to_be_done: hotstuff_rs is a fork, so extend the Network trait with a push-style receive: give LibP2PNetwork a `std::sync::mpsc::Sender<(VerifyingKey, ProgressMessage)>` (and one for block-sync requests/responses) that `enqueue_inbound` (swarm.rs:2985-3000) sends on directly, and have `start_polling` (receiving.rs:44-76) return those receivers instead of spawning the poller thread that loops `network.recv()` (bridge.rs:680-682: Mutex<VecDeque>::pop_front) and sleeps 250 us when empty. `ProgressMessageStub::recv` (receiving.rs:171-186) already blocks on `recv_timeout`, so the view-aware buffering is untouched. Keep the old poll path as the default impl for other Network implementations (tests).
ideas.reasoning: Every consensus message today crosses: swarm thread -> Mutex<VecDeque> -> poller thread (parked up to 250 us, then a scheduler wake) -> std mpsc -> algo thread (another wake). The critical path of a view crosses that at least 3-4 times (header at each follower, two PhaseVotes at the next leader, BlockDataResponse at each follower). At idle the l3 attribution measured the whole delivery stack at 0.5-2 ms, of which the park is ~125 us avg; under load on a host running 3 nodes x (exec pool + 9 verify threads + rocksdb bg + 8 root workers) a parked thread's wake is scheduler-bound (s46 measured 19-41 ms/blk of runqueue wait on the HotStuff thread), so 0.3-1.5 ms per crossing is plausible. 3-4 crossings x 0.3-1.5 ms = 1-6 ms of a ~620 ms view -> +0.2-1.0% blk/s, x0.6 late-window dilution -> +0.1-0.6% matched/s. Small, but it also removes one thread per node and one mutex from the hot path.

ideas.risk: Low. Must preserve the S370 no-spin guarantee (a blocking channel does) and the inbound cap semantics (MAX_INBOUND_QUEUE=10,000 becomes a sync_channel bound or a counter). The block_data_inbound / native_da queues can stay as they are.
ideas.why_new: Not in the s64 list; the l3 doc proposed only a condvar for the park (keeps the extra thread and hop) and ranked it for idle. This removes the hop entirely and is aimed at the loaded regime where thread wake latency, not the 250 us park, is the cost.

ideas.title: Direct-path frame hygiene: skip zstd and the fresh compression context for sub-1 KB consensus frames (votes, requests, ACKs) and reuse a thread-local compressor for the large ones
ideas.area: torus-network codec.rs
ideas.what_needs_to_be_done: In write_length_prefixed_borsh_zstd (codec.rs:265-285) and its response twin: (1) keep a thread-local `zstd::bulk::Compressor` (level 3) instead of `zstd::bulk::compress`, which creates and frees a ZSTD_CCtx per call; (2) for payloads under ~1 KB (PhaseVote ~200 B, BlockDataRequest ~80 B, ProposalHeader ~400 B, DirectResponse 0 B) write a zstd 'raw block' or, if the /2.0 framing must stay, compress with level 1 — the 15x ratio comes only from the body pushes; (3) optionally reply to /torus/direct requests before the inner handling instead of after (the ACK is not on the consensus critical path but the responder's zstd + write currently sits on the swarm thread inside the request handler, swarm.rs:1455-1560).
ideas.reasoning: Per view on the direct path there are ~2 PhaseVotes, 2 BlockDataRequests, 2 BlockDataResponses (8 KB CompactBlock) and their 6 ACKs, plus timeout traffic: ~12-16 frames/view, each paying a CCtx create/free plus a zstd call (~20-50 us) on the swarm thread of the sender or receiver. That is ~0.3-0.8 ms of swarm-thread time per view spread over three nodes, and each large push frame pays a multi-hundred-KB workspace allocation per call. On this bench this is worth well under 1% of the view; it matters more for the WAN/production regime (more validators -> more frames per view) than for throughput here. Listed because it is a one-file change with zero protocol impact, not because it moves the headline.

ideas.expected_improvement: +0-0.3% (swarm-thread CPU only; ~0.3-0.8 ms per view host-wide)
ideas.risk: Wire compatibility: /2.0 frames must still decompress on old binaries, so use zstd raw/uncompressed blocks or level 1 rather than a new framing; a thread-local compressor must not be shared across tokio worker threads without Send care.
ideas.why_new: No s64 item touches the direct codec; the previous encoding explorer looked at body/attest encoding, not the per-frame compressor lifecycle or the ACK frames.

raw.notes:
Headline for this angle: consensus-message encoding is NOT a lever on this devnet. Measured on val0 (s65-votefix-ctl-r1, metrics-after): torus_validate_block_decode_seconds 0.0194 s / 1115 calls = 17 us per CompactBlock decode; the datum is ~6.5 KB (200 x 32-byte action hashes, torus-types lib.rs:479-484) plus a ~400 B header/justify, so borsh/bincode of proposals, headers, votes and BlockDataResponse is <0.01% of a 620 ms view. The body-level encoding costs that do matter are all already in the s64 list: attest re-serialization 3.57 s/312 = 11.4 ms per validate (section 5 'attest over action hashes'), commit_body_encode 3.14 s/1569 = 2.0 ms per commit (section 5 'move the commit-time body write'), da_reconstruct 15.0 s/312 = 48 ms (item 10).

Evidence that changes existing estimates: (1) native_gossip_received_actions_total on val1 and val2 is exactly 107,294 = every action val0 admitted, so s64 item 10 (pool-first body reconstruction) can assume a 100% pool hit rate on followers, and the 'hash-only push' item should be read as 'push off' for the bench (see idea 1). (2) qc_collect is measured from our Propose until the PC for our block reaches us via the NEXT leader's justify (view_metrics.rs:109-121), so its 260-300 ms includes the next leader's build; there is no unexplained transport gap — message transport is at most a few ms per hop. (3) RocksDB per node per run: WAL 12.5-13.0 GB, flush 1.76-1.87 GB, compaction CPU 258-263 s (~0.65 core each, ~2 cores host-wide); the numbers are near-identical on all three nodes although only val0 takes RPC, so the WAL is dominated by exec/commit/mirror writes, not ingest. Storage is not blocking the HotStuff thread (s65 wchan) but compaction CPU is a host-wide tax worth keeping in mind for any CPU-contention idea (renice item). (4) docs/l3-arrival-attribution.md already ranks TORUS_CONSENSUS_DIRECT_FAN=1 for the loaded regime; it has never been A/B'd under load (torus_consensus_direct_fan_sent_total 0 in every s65 cell). Bounded gain: a header queues behind at most one native batch on the gossipsub substream, and at 343 actions/s with the 50 ms flush timer (swarm.rs:660) a batch is ~17 actions x 19 KB ~= 330 KB ~= ~1 ms on loopback, so expect <= +0.3%; still a free env-only arm.

Not bugs, for the record: consensus_mesh_peers reads 0 on val0 and 1 on val1/val2 because validators are gossipsub explicit peers ('GRAFT: ignoring request from direct peer' at 02:59:21 in val0.log.gz); explicit peers receive every publish/forward outside the mesh, so delivery is unaffected. HotStuffMessage::size() (hotstuff messages.rs ~115) uses mem::size_of, so ProgressMessageBuffer capacity accounting ignores heap data (harmless today, would matter if bodies ever ride the progress queue). PhaseCertificate::is_correct re-verifies 3 ed25519 signatures with a fresh borsh alloc each (types.rs:149-175) at 3-4 sites per view (implementation.rs:1903, 2325, 1437-1440, 1537): ~0.5 ms per view; memoizing per (block, view, phase) is ~0.1% and not worth a separate idea.

Memory 841d7e571c71a434 (July 23) had already flagged 'bulk-body decode on the swarm loop' and 'double DA mirror per gossip-ingested action'; the inline double mirror was fixed, but the push-path mirror-before-dedup described in idea 1 is the surviving form of it.

ideas.title: Move 4 MB body/push (de)serialization off the single swarm task (spawn_blocking decode/encode for payloads > 64 KB)
ideas.area: torus-network swarm loop (crates/torus-network/src/swarm.rs handle_event / handle_consensus_direct_traced / send_direct_observed / decode_pre_proposal_batch)
ideas.what_needs_to_be_done: Today every /torus/direct request is handled inline on the one swarm task: (1) handle_consensus_direct_traced does Message::try_from_slice on the full ~3.9 MB BlockDataResponse (swarm.rs ~L3207-3240); (2) the pre-proposal FULL-BODY push is bincode-decoded inline via decode_pre_proposal_batch (swarm.rs L174-179, call site in the Direct Request arm ~L1520-1535) — 3.3-4.0 MB per proposal at cap 200, then 200 channel sends; (3) send_direct_observed borsh-encodes the 3.9 MB response with message.try_to_vec() on the swarm task (swarm.rs ~L2797) before send_request. Change: in the Direct Request arm, if request.payload.len() > ~64 KB hand the bytes to tokio::task::spawn_blocking (or a small rayon pool) that decodes and then calls enqueue_consensus_inbound / the native_action_inbound sends; keep small messages (votes, headers, AdvanceView, TimeoutVote) inline so their ordering and latency are untouched. For the outbound side, carry BlockDataResponse bytes pre-encoded (encode once on the algo thread or in pending_bodies as Bytes) so send_direct only wraps them; DirectRequest must still be sent from the swarm task (send_request needs &mut swarm), so only the encode moves. Preserve per-peer ordering of body responses only (they are idempotent; hotstuff drops untracked duplicates). Validate with the existing TORUS_SWARM_POLL_TRACE=1 poll-duration aggregates (swarm_poll_trace.rs) plus header-delivery and body-transfer legs from body_fetch_diag admission stamps, 3+3 cells.
ideas.reasoning: Counted in the s65-votefix-ctl-r2 load window (246 s, 390 views, 3 nodes): 1256 BlockDataResponse admissions (3.9 MB each, 4.9 GB) and 780 push receives (1.458 GB pushed = 3.75 MB per proposal, decoded on both followers). Per view that is ~3.2 body encodes on the leader's swarm task, ~3.2 body decodes and 2 push decodes on follower swarm tasks — ~11 MB of borsh/bincode (de)serialization per node per view. Using the only measured decode cost in hand (validate_block da_reconstruct = 200 bincode decodes + MultiGet = 36-46 ms), a 4 MB decode is ~15-25 ms and an encode ~10-15 ms, so each node's swarm task is blocked ~40-55 ms per ~600 ms view (7-9%). While blocked it cannot forward the header, votes, body requests or AdvanceView of that node. The cross-node timeline shows exactly the tails such blocking produces: header delivery L->F p50 10.7 / p90 47 / mean 19 ms; body request-admit -> response-admit p50 16 / p90 69 / mean 30 ms; vote transit p90 97 ms. Removing ~40-55 ms of swarm-task occupancy per view should pull the means toward the medians: header −5..−8 ms, vote/request −5..−10 ms, body transfer −5..−10 ms = −15..−28 ms per 600 ms view (2.5-4.5%). With the s64 0.6x late-window dilution: +1.5-2.7% matched/s; call it +1-3%.

ideas.title: Stop the redundant body fetch traffic: 61% extra BlockDataRequests and 38% duplicate 3.9 MB responses per view
ideas.area: hotstuff_rs algorithm loop + body retry (crates/hotstuff_rs/src/algorithm.rs poll_progress_and_retry; hotstuff/implementation.rs tick_pending_body_retries_at, tick_missing_pc_block_fetch, tick_justify_fetch_retries) and the network hand-off (torus-network bridge/swarm enqueue_inbound)
ideas.what_needs_to_be_done: Two mechanisms produce the waste. (a) Retry-before-drain: algorithm.rs poll_progress_and_retry runs tick_body_retries() BEFORE pm_stub.recv(), so when the consensus thread returns to the loop after >100 ms (busy or asleep) it re-requests a body whose response is already admitted in shared.inbound / the mpsc (BODY_RETRY_INTERVAL = 100 ms, implementation.rs L2988). (b) Double-fire: 112 of 470 inter-request gaps are < 5 ms — two fetch paths (pending-body retry and the S432/S426 by-hash fetches) fire for the same hash in one tick. Fix: (1) expose a cheap `Network::admitted_body_hashes()` (a HashSet<[u8;32]> in SharedState updated in enqueue_inbound/enqueue_body_fetch_traced_stages and cleared when the poller pops) and skip a re-request when the hash is already admitted; (2) make the by-hash fetch paths share body_fetch_tracker's last_req so one hash gets one request per interval; (3) as a zero-code first step, A/B the existing TORUS_BODY_BEFORE_EXPIRY=1 (recv_before_body_retry, receiving.rs ~L200-245; docs/perf/body-before-expiry-experiment-2026-09-18.md says it was never measured live), which drains the queued body before the retry tick. Score by adm_request/adm_response counts per view from TORUS_BODY_FETCH_TRACE=1 and by direct wire bytes (torus_wire_compression_bytes{path=direct}).
ideas.reasoning: Load window of s65-votefix-ctl-r2: 1258 request admissions and 1256 response admissions for 390 views x 2 followers = 780 needed, i.e. 478 extra requests (61%) and 477 responses received with tracked_header=false (38% of all responses). Requests per (leader,follower,view): 1x 482, 2x 189, 3x 88, 4x 17, 5x 6, 6x 6. Each extra response costs: clone of the 3.9 MB block on the leader's algo thread (~2 ms), borsh encode on the leader's swarm task (~12 ms), zstd-3 compress on a tokio worker (3.9 MB at ~100-150 MB/s = 25-40 ms), decompress (~5 ms), borsh decode on the follower's swarm task (~20 ms), poller + mpsc hop, then dropped. That is ~65-80 ms CPU per view host-wide (~0.10-0.13 of a core) and ~12 ms/view of swarm-task blocking on the leader plus ~20 ms on a follower. On this host (runqueue 41-48 on 18 CPUs, hotstuff-algo rq_wait 85-105 ms per block) freed CPU translates to view time; s64 valued ~0.35-0.4 core of relief at +5-15%, so ~0.12 core is worth +0.5-1.5%, plus the swarm-task un-blocking (~1/3 of idea 1's effect). Duplicate 4 MB responses also sit ahead of votes in the next leader's FIFO (body_rx_dup preceded the QC-forming vote in 4 views).

ideas.title: Wake-on-enqueue for the hotstuff poller: drop the 250 us sleep-poll hop between the swarm task and hotstuff-algo

Replace the poll with a wake: add `Network::recv_timeout(&mut self, d: Duration)` (default impl = recv + sleep, so other Network impls keep working) backed by a Condvar in SharedState that enqueue_inbound notifies; or, simpler, let LibP2PNetwork own the progress Sender and have enqueue_inbound push straight into the three demux channels, deleting the poller thread. Every inbound consensus message therefore pays: up to 250 us sleep + 50 us timer slack + one runqueue wait for the poller (~0.1-0.4 ms) + a second wake of hotstuff-algo. Critical path per view has ~5 such hops (header at the followers, vote at the next leader, body request at the leader, body response at the follower, AdvanceView): 5 x 0.5-0.8 ms = 2.5-4 ms of a ~600 ms view (0.4-0.7%), plus 3 x 4.5% = 0.135 core freed on a host where consensus threads already wait 85-105 ms per block on the runqueue. ideas.title: Zero-code network-loop A/B: TORUS_CONSENSUS_DIRECT_FAN=1 (+GOSSIP_MIRROR=0) and TORUS_HASH_ONLY_PUSH_THRESHOLD=1
ideas.area: torus-network config knobs (config.rs consensus_direct_fan/consensus_gossip_mirror; bridge.rs hash_only_push_threshold) — harness env only
ideas.what_needs_to_be_done: Two restart-only levers that test the gossip-queue and swarm-task hypotheses before any code: (1) TORUS_CONSENSUS_DIRECT_FAN=1 with TORUS_CONSENSUS_GOSSIP_MIRROR=0 on all three validators (flip together; consensus_dedup guards the mixed state) so headers/AdvanceView/TimeoutVote go over /torus/direct request_response instead of gossipsub, whose per-peer queue (512 deep, shared with the native-action topic) and Strict-mode ed25519 sign/verify sit on every header today; (2) TORUS_HASH_ONLY_PUSH_THRESHOLD=1 so the pre-proposal push is the 6.4 KB hash manifest (0xFC) instead of the 3.3-4.0 MB full body set (0xFD) that is currently pushed on every proposal because the direct-push floor was raised to 8 MB; receivers then run plan_prewarm_requests (200 NativeDaStore::contains reads) and pull nothing since gossip already delivered every action (val1/val2 native_gossip_received_actions_total = 126,530 = all published). Run 3 control + 3 per arm interleaved at cap 200, score header delivery (body_fetch_diag header admission at followers minus the leader's self-admission), the push_rx count, gossip-verify pool CPU (threads.log torus-gossip-ve*), and matched/s.
ideas.reasoning: (1) Header delivery leader->followers is p50 10.7 / mean 19.2 / p90 47 ms on a loopback host where a QUIC hop is <1 ms; on the leader the header is published into gossipsub behind up to 512 queued 128 KB native batches per peer (val0 publishes ~77 batches/s: 23k messages per 300 s) and each message is signed and verified. The direct fan is the same path votes use, and vote transit tracks the body-request transit in the median (−2.7 ms difference), so headers should fall to ~5-10 ms mean: −7..−11 ms per ~600 ms view = 1.2-1.8% view time, +0.7-1.1% matched/s after dilution. (2) The full-body push costs per proposal: bincode encode of 3.75 MB on the pre-proposal thread, 2 x zstd compress (25-40 ms each on tokio workers), and on each follower decompress + bincode decode on the swarm task (push sent -> 'received pre-proposal action batch' = 46-75 ms in the raw trace) + 200 dedup ingests through the gossip-verify pool (trust-cache key = EIP-712 encode + keccak, ~0.15 ms each = 30 ms per follower). That is ~100-140 ms CPU per view host-wide (~0.2 core) and ~20 ms/view of swarm-task blocking per follower, all redundant with gossip. Worth +0.5-2% by the same CPU-relief scaling as idea 2. Surprises and evidence that changes existing estimates (all from s65-votefix-ctl-r2, code at wt/s63-body-fetch f05b20e, read-only):

1. Consensus thread asleep with a 4 MB body already queued. Cross-node timeline (all three nodes share the host clock) over the load window: 294 of 1250 body pickups (response admitted at the network layer -> body_fetch_diag receive on hotstuff-algo) took >100 ms, 172 took >300 ms, summing to 119.5 s of queue time across 3 nodes in a 246 s window. Inside those gaps the 10 Hz wchan sampler shows the algo thread R 658 samples vs S futex_wait_queue 268; in 35 of 293 gaps every sample was S (asleep the whole time). Example: val1 processed header 781 at 03:45:00.147, sent vote+request by .163, the response was admitted at .179, and hotstuff-algo (tid 855508) was S futex at .197/.305/.443 and logged nothing until .454 — while its poller thread cycled ~2,000 times/s that second (threads.log 05:45:00 local: 1,996 cswch/s), so the hop was not starved. The vote persist was already done (the request had left). Something after the header handler blocks on a futex for ~290 ms (candidates: a RocksDB write-group wait behind the exec/trade writers, or the exec dispatch sync_channel; not the recv). This is not attributable from logs; the cheapest decisive instrumentation is a per-loop-stage atomic 'where am I' on hotstuff-algo read by the host sampler (an upgrade of s64 #9). It also means planned item (A) may not be the only vote-path sleeper.

2. qc_collect decomposition (what the 260-300 ms actually is): from the leader's header self-admission, first body request admitted at the leader p50 37.5 ms (delivery 10.7 + vote ~25); last PhaseVote processed at the next leader (QC) p50 78 ms, mean 125, p90 291; QC -> produce_block at the next leader p50 161 ms, mean 211, p90 451. So the vote/QC leg is fast in the median and the next leader's body validate+insert+commit dominates — this supports s64 #1/#8/#10 and says the network loop is a tail problem (p90s), not a median one. In late-QC views (>150 ms, 65 of 240), the event preceding the QC-forming vote on the next leader was another message handler (39), on_committed_block (18) or validate_block (7), with p50 74 ms / p90 264 ms from that event to the vote: the commit feed on a FOLLOWER delays QC formation at the next leader, which s64 #1 (leader-only deferral) does not cover — though since produce waits for the body anyway, the gain is fewer timeouts rather than a shorter chain step.

3. Thread accounting correction: the host sampler threads.log columns are (%usr %system %guest %wait %CPU CPU cswch/s nvcswch/s); an earlier reading of it as %CPU=col8 was wrong. Corrected per node: hotstuff-algo 17.8-18.4% CPU, 9.6-10.2% runqueue wait, 61 voluntary / 101-107 involuntary switches/s (preempted every ~1.8 ms of CPU); 18 tokio-rt-worker threads at 2.2% each (~40% of a core), each waiting 4.9% of the time on the runqueue at 64 wakeups/s (~0.77 ms per wake); futures-timer 0.8-0.9% CPU, 212-278 wakeups/s; poller 4.5% CPU. Timestamps in threads.log are local (UTC+2).

4. s65-zerocode-ctl-r1 is a blown cell (matched/s 5,011, load-window view 2.37 s, agree=DISAGREE, 3.8 GB logs) and should be excluded from any control average; its host sampler was the one first inspected here.

5. Gossip dedup is invisible at the app layer: val1/val2 received exactly 126,530 native actions each (gossipsub de-duplicates by message id before Event::Message), so whether the 3-node mesh forwards each 128 KB batch a second time (4 wire copies for 2 useful deliveries) cannot be read from torus counters; only libp2p's internal gossipsub metrics or per-socket byte counters would show it. Not claimed as an idea for that reason.

6. Redundancy summary for the CPU-relief ledger (per view, host-wide, cap 200): 1.2 duplicate 3.9 MB body responses (~65-80 ms CPU), a 3.75 MB full-body push decoded twice plus 400 duplicate ingests (~100-140 ms CPU), poller sleep-polling (~4.5% of a core per node). ideas.what_needs_to_be_done: Today every view v gets an ABSOLUTE deadline epoch_start + max_view_time * multiplier * (v - start + 1) (crates/hotstuff_rs/src/pacemaker/implementation.rs:836-841 and :891-900). `update_view` (:556-640) rebases only when the entered view is > 2 slots AHEAD (:610) and stretches only when the stall multiplier > 1 (:625-633); a healthy QC-driven entry (depth 0) inherits the absolute slot. With loaded views of ~620 ms against the 500 ms slot (devnet/genesis.json:8) the replica is behind schedule, so `tick()` (:103-165) fires a timeout on the very next loop iteration: TimeoutVote broadcast, update_view(v+1) with depth 1 -> deadline now + 1 s; leader(v) never proposes. Change: (a) in update_view treat `scheduled < now` as stale too and rebase from now (mirror of the S395 ahead-rebase), so every entry route (QC, TC, timeout) gets deadline = entry + slot; (b) make the slot load-adaptive: slot = max(timeout_base_ms, k x EWMA of recent header->QC latency, e.g. k=2, capped), a Jolteon/DiemBFT-style timer, computed from consensus-visible timestamps so all honest replicas agree within jitter; (c) keep the exponential backoff for views that genuinely fail. STRUCTURAL FINDING (the angle's main answer): the hotstuff-algo thread is not lock-bound. wchan (10 Hz, s65-votefix-ctl-r1): 69% S futex_wait_queue, 29% R, 0.5% D (ext4 journal: do_get_write_access / wait_transaction_locked, i.e. WAL appends). pidstat: 17.8% on-CPU, 9.4% runqueue wait, 55 voluntary + 98 involuntary switches/s. Inventory of everything the thread can block on: (1) `ProgressMessageStub::recv` -> std mpsc recv_timeout (receiving.rs:177-189) = the futex; (2) the network poller thread hop: swarm pushes into Mutex<VecDeque> `inbound` (swarm.rs:2984), a poller thread polls it with a 250 us sleep (receiving.rs:45-74) and forwards over a second channel — two wake-ups per message, ~0.6 ms scheduler latency each on this host, ~3 ms/view, not worth a separate idea; (3) mempool RwLock held only for insert / evict / select-clone / remove (lib.rs:594-598, 874-891, 942-947); (4) exec_pipeline's sync_channel(0) rendezvous is exec-thread<->flush-worker only (exec_pipeline.rs:193), never the consensus thread; (5) exec_tx sync_channel(64) blocking send is never hit (torus_exec_dispatch_deferred_total 0, exec_queue_depth 0 in fix-r1); (6) pre_proposal_tx sync_channel(4) uses try_send (app.rs:4702); (7) Network send/broadcast are unbounded tokio channel sends (bridge.rs:665-676); (8) RocksDB writes use default WriteOptions, no fsync (kv_store.rs:142-166). Three threads each ~29% running sums to ~0.87: at any instant about one consensus thread in the fleet is running — the wait is the cross-node serial chain, which is what planned item C and s64 items 1/5/10 attack.

INSTANCE-LEVEL COST OF THAT CHAIN IS 2-3x THE MEANS: leader(626)=val2: QC formed 03:01:00.805 -> body picked up 01.023 (207 ms of thread busy while the body sat in the inbound queue) -> validate 567 -> produce_block called 01.309 -> selected 01.581 -> pre-proposal push 01.664 -> commit feeds for 565/566 02.190-02.306 -> header admitted 02.484: 1.68 s propose delay vs the 380 ms mean. This supports the planned move of the commit feed (C) and the s64 pre-builder idea, and shows why views time out under the x2 backoff.

HEADER DELIVERY IS NOT THE TAIL: cross-node header admission skew per view (body_fetch_diag admission kind=header unix_us, 473 views): p50 10 ms, p90 46, p99 164, max 358 ms; only 1 view > 300 ms. The s64 UDP-buffer item can at most shave the ~14 ms mean.

EVIDENCE THAT CHANGES EXISTING ESTIMATES: (a) consensus_timeout_total (141-169 per node per 300 s) is ~75% instant view skips (torus_view_duration le=0.008 bucket 104-114 views per node) caused by the absolute pacemaker schedule; 'views per committed block 1.6' is mostly free skips, so the s55 'raise timeout_base_ms -> views/block 1.50->1.07 but matched/s flat' null result was expected and does not rule out deadline changes for the ~36 real timeouts per node. (b) The s64 item 9 wchan sampler as configured cannot separate lock waits from channel waits (both are futex_wait_queue); the pidstat cswch/nvcswch columns are the better signal and were misread earlier in my pass (pidstat -h columns: $8 %wait, $9 %CPU, $11 cswch/s, $12 nvcswch/s). (c) commit_persist_write p50 ~25 ms for ~4 MB under load (fix-r1 val0) = ~160 MB/s effective, consistent with write-group queueing behind the trade writer / flush worker rather than memcpy cost, which raises the value of the s64 'move the 4 MB body-record write off the consensus thread' and 'trade writer disable_wal' items.

POSSIBLE BUGS: (1) duplicate body fetches/validates (idea 1) — 34-48% extra requests, 60% extra responses, 15% of heights validated twice. (2) `torus_vote_state_write_seconds` (s65 item A timer, kv_store.rs:139-166) does not appear in s65-votefix-fix-r1/metrics-after-val0.txt; the item-A owner should check the registration before trusting that A/B. (3) The `on_receive_msg` info log (implementation.rs:860-864) prints the LOCAL view for every HotStuff message; it is the only per-message log and was enough to rebuild per-view timelines here — worth keeping but pacemaker events (TimeoutVote/AdvanceView) are not logged, which is why real timeouts vs skips had to be inferred from histogram buckets.

CAVEATS: all counts are from one control cell (s65-votefix-ctl-r1, val0 unless stated); within-arm CV is 2-7% so the +1-3% items need n>=3 to detect; the pacemaker estimate rests on an inferred split of the 1.2-2 s views.

1) Planned item C scope: the commit feed runs on TWO paths, and the log shows the QC-holder path is the one that actually commits in the common case: on_receive_phase_vote (implementation.rs:1469-1476 block_tree.update + process_update_result) runs BEFORE the AdvanceView broadcast (:1503-1510) and before the view advances. s65-votefix-fix-r1 val0: third vote for 810 at 02:52:10.831 -> on_commit_block fired 10.832 -> feeds until 10.996 -> only then AdvanceView; peers sat in view 810 the whole time. In all four of val0's skipped leader slots (805, 808, 811, 835) the slot followed a late third vote plus a 165-400 ms feed. If C only moves the feed in enter_view (:637-643, the s64 V1 location) the burn interaction stays; at minimum the AdvanceView broadcast should precede process_update_result in on_receive_phase_vote (3-line reorder). The worktree currently has uncommitted edits implementing C (inline self-header, leader_feed_order_test.rs); I read HEAD f05b20e and did not verify what those edits cover.
2) Possible bug / open question: view 811 was val0's slot (round-robin view mod 3 == 1 holds for every other view in 794-846); val0 formed QC(810), finished its feed at 10.996, yet never called produce_block or broadcast any 811 header, and the next header (812, val2) came at 11.903; val2 produced 812 at 11.431, i.e. the peers' 811 deadline was ~400 ms after entry, so a simple 'deadline already past' does not explain val0's silence. No enter_view error, no missing-parent fetch, no RECOVER lines (none are logged), exec-backpressure yield is OFF by default. Candidates: 810->812 jump via a TC(811) that val0 amplified while still in 810 (Bracha f=0, :296-313), or a create_proposal_based_on_tc RECOVER (case 5, :763-833) with an unavailable tip. Pacemaker events are not logged (main.rs:812 log_events(false)); one cell with ViewTimeout/CollectTC/ReceiveAdvanceView/StartView logging would settle it and is the cheapest next diagnostic for the 1.5 views/block problem. 55 of 522 load-window views had no header at all on val0; 119 of 467 proposals never committed.
3) Evidence for existing items: header->body-response is 97 ms mean on val0 (n=307), consistent with s64 item 8's -50-70 ms estimate; the third vote is processed 110 ms after the first on average because it lands while validate+insert (50-170 ms) holds the thread, but vote prioritisation would not help since the body insert is needed before proposing anyway. Body responses wait in the inbound queue 18.5 ms mean (n=462), 23 waited >100 ms, 13 >200 ms (thread busy in feed/validate).
4) Bracha amplification threshold at n=3 is f=0, so the earliest replica's absolute schedule governs every view's effective deadline; with entry-time skew of the per-replica epoch_start_time this shortens the effective budget below 500 ms. Relevant to idea 1's validation.
5) Pacemaker tick step 3 (:194-215) always broadcasts a second AdvanceView for a PC that on_receive_phase_vote already broadcast (last_advance_view is not shared); each peer then re-verifies 3 ed25519 signatures and rebroadcasts once. Negligible CPU, but it doubles AdvanceView traffic per QC; folds into idea 2.
6) s55 memory cd44df5b539c9110 (timeout 500->1500 at cap 100: views/blk 1.50->1.07, ms/blk -20% +/-50%, 'do not tune timeouts') is the closest prior to idea 1; the point estimate was favourable and the null verdict rests on a 40%-CV exec-bound regime. Today's CV is 2-7% and consensus is the limit, so the family is worth one clean re-test; I rate idea 1 low confidence because of that history.
