ideas.what_needs_to_be_done: Today one 400-order PlaceOrderBatch is canonically re-encoded and keccak'd 3-4 times per node and deep-cloned twice at ingest. RPC path (val0): (1) `verify_one_action_with` (crates/torus-rpc/src/torus.rs:296-307) re-serializes the whole action as serde_json (~60-80 KB) and keccaks it only to produce the acknowledgement hash; (2) `add_native_action_presigned` (crates/torus-mempool/src/lib.rs:410-413) does `action.clone()` for the insert, then `mirror_to_da` clones it again into the pending buffer (lib.rs:756-762) and `gossip_native_action` bincode-encodes it (lib.rs:542); (3) `submit_native_action_inner` computes `verified_cache_key` (lib.rs:583 = canonical bytes + keccak) and then, INSIDE `self.native.write()`, `insert_verified` computes `compute_action_hash` (canonical bytes + keccak again) plus `bincode::serialized_size` (crates/torus-mempool/src/native_pool.rs:157-164); (4) the DA flush recomputes `compute_action_hash_with_scratch` and re-bincodes every body (crates/torus-state/src/native_da.rs:96-98). Gossip path (val1/val2): `add_native_action_from_gossip` (lib.rs:432-448) mirrors (clone) first, computes the cache key once for the lookup (always a miss for a fresh action: `torus_verified_sender_cache_misses_total` = 121,367 on val1 = every gossiped action), recovers, then `admit_gossip` -> `submit_native_action_inner` computes the cache key a second time and the pool hash a third time; and the network thread already had the exact DA value bytes (`bincode(action)` = `action_bytes[20..]` of the `(Address, SignedNativeAction)` tuple, crates/torus-network/src/swarm.rs:1357-1366) but discards them. Change: (a) in the verify closure build the canonical preimage once (`append_canonical_bytes`, torus-types/src/lib.rs:933-946 and :988-1000 share it) and derive both `compute_action_hash` and `verified_cache_key` from it; return the content hash as the RPC acknowledgement instead of keccak(JSON) (the bench never reads the ack value: tools/bench-throughput/src/main.rs:1440-1447 only checks that `hash` is present; update the two tests at torus-rpc/src/lib.rs:1194 and :1258); (b) add `insert_verified_with_hash(sender, action, hash, cache_key, encoded_len)` so nothing is hashed under the pool write lock; (c) make `mirror_to_da` take `(hash, Bytes)` — on the RPC path the bytes are the same bincode buffer the gossip publish needs (`bincode(&(sender, action))` = 20-byte address || `bincode(action)`), on the gossip path forward the received slice from swarm.rs:1357 alongside the decoded pair — and have `put_batch` accept pre-hashed, pre-encoded bodies; (d) remove the `action.clone()` at lib.rs:410 (mirror and gossip no longer borrow the action). ideas.title: Explain the 640 ms client-side hold vs 26 ms server-side handler time; total the generator's silent 429/timeout errors; align CONC with the 64-request cap

ideas.what_needs_to_be_done: (1) Little's law on the generator: CONC=256 permits (run-cell.sh:124, semaphore at bench main.rs:2385/2631/2701) at 398 accepted/s means each permit is held ~640 ms, yet the server-side `torus_rpc_request_duration_seconds` on val0 has mean 25.9 ms, p50 ~12 ms, p99 ~200 ms, max < 0.82 s, and Little's law on the server side gives only ~10.5 requests inside the JSON-RPC handler. Roughly 600 ms per request is spent outside the handler (client runtime, TCP, hyper body read, or requests that never return) and nobody measures it. (2) jsonrpsee 0.26 takes one ConnectionGuard permit per HTTP request and answers 429 immediately when 64 are busy (~/.cargo/registry/src/*/jsonrpsee-server-0.26.0/src/server.rs:1028-1029); the node default is 64 (crates/torus-rpc/src/lib.rs:45) and no campaign script sets TORUS_RPC_MAX_CONNS, while the generator runs 256 concurrent submits. A 429 body is not JSON, so it surfaces as 'parse: error decoding response body' — exactly the 5 lines in bench.log — and `submit_payloads` counts it in SUBMIT_ERRS but neither retries it nor ever prints the total (bench main.rs:1462-1493); reqwest also has a 10 s timeout (main.rs:2191) whose expiries are equally invisible. Each lost fire wasted a 400-order EIP-712 signing on the generator (1.45 cores). Do: print SUBMIT_ERRS by class (429 / timeout / rpc error) and client-side submit latency percentiles at the end of every cell; add an HTTP-level counter on the node for 429s and a timer from hyper accept/body-read to JSON-RPC dispatch (or a jsonrpsee HTTP middleware) so the accept-to-dispatch gap is attributed; set CONC <= TORUS_RPC_MAX_CONNS (either CONC=64 or MAX_CONNS=256) in run-cell.sh; optionally try SUBMIT=4-8 (run-cell.sh:24 default 1) to cut per-request HTTP/spawn_blocking/rayon-install overhead on the 4-worker RPC runtime (main.rs:944-946).

Either most permits are held by requests that are not in the handler (client-side scheduling on a host with load1 33-44, or 10 s timeouts: 5% of requests timing out would pin ~200 of the 256 permits), or a large share of fires are 429'd and dropped. In the first case the real submit RTT is ~25x the handler time and the knee sweep will move the wrong knob; in the second the generator's signing CPU is partly wasted and 'submitted' undercounts fires. Arithmetic: 256 / 398 per s = 0.643 s per permit; server 3148 s of handler time / 300 s = 10.5 in flight; 0.643 - 0.026 = 0.617 s unaccounted per request. If SUBMIT=8 is adopted after the accounting is fixed: rpc-worker CPU is 1.33 ms per request of which ~0.4-0.6 ms is per-request HTTP/JSON-RPC/response overhead, so 350 fewer requests/s saves ~0.15-0.2 cores plus ~700 fewer spawn_blocking/rayon wake-ups per second — ~1% of host CPU, +0-1% matched/s.

raw.notes:
Answer to the angle's question: per node, each action is verified exactly once today (RPC ingress on val0; gossip recover on val1/val2, which seeds the exec trust cache so exec hits ~100%). That is already the BFT minimum for independent validation, and the alternatives do not work here: (a) trusted-validator attestation (accept the gossipsub-authenticated publisher's claimed sender, `add_native_action_from_gossip_trusted`, verified_locally=false) would move the ~2 ms/action recover onto the exec thread as cache misses: 192 x 2 ms / 8 rayon threads ≈ 50 ms wall per block on the thread that is 0.86 busy, the same mechanism as the s375 cache-OFF result (exec_verify ~360 ms/block, -38% throughput); (b) seeding another node's trust cache from an attestation would make a wrong attestation a consensus fork (the cache doc lib.rs:181-190 is explicit); (c) leader-only verification with fraud proofs is unusable for a DEX because matched fills cannot be reverted after the fact. What IS avoidable is the hashing around the recover (ideas 1-2) and the storage churn of the mirror (idea 3).

Quantified CPU (ctl-r2 load window, pidstat threads.log): gossip re-verify = 1.04 core per follower (2.8 ms per 400-order action at 369 actions/s), 2.2 cores host-wide; ingress verify 1.06 core on val0; total verification-related 3.3 of 18 cores (18%), the largest thread group on the box, ahead of rocksdb:low (2.0 cores). No perf doc had this attribution. Because it is off the consensus thread, its throughput effect is only through the run queue (HotStuff runqueue wait 90-105 ms/block per s64), so even eliminating it entirely would be worth roughly +3-4%, not more.

Evidence that changes existing estimates: (1) s64 'exec verify 44 ms/block despite 0 misses' is 54 ms/block in ctl-r2 (18.66 s / 344) and is the sequential per-action key hashing at eip712.rs:1100-1110, not the rayon phase, so the s64 fix (skip rayon at 100% hit) would recover little of it; idea 1 covers both. (2) The gossip-path pre-recover trust-cache lookup (lib.rs:441, T2.1) misses 100% of the time in every valid cell (misses == received: 110724, 129470/129464, 82751/82746, 107295/107294, 121367/121366) because gossipsub never echoes a node's own publish and only val0 ingests; it costs a full 21 KB encode+keccak per action for nothing. (3) 'Verify only what will be selected' on followers (priority-ordered lazy verify) would save the 37% expiring share of the 2.2 cores (~0.8 core) but is subsumed by planned item B, which shrinks the gossip stream at the source. (4) Gossipsub forwarding in the 3-node mesh is redundant (each follower re-forwards val0's batches to the other follower, ~2.2 GB/cell per direction of duplicates dropped by the seen-cache after Strict-mode signature checks), but the CPU is only ~0.03 core per follower; no slow-peer failures in valid cells, so not worth a change at n=3.

Possible bug / robustness: s65-zerocode-ctl-r1 (status INVALID in summary.json) shows val0 native_gossip_dropped_full 39,723 (22% of admitted actions never gossiped; outbound channel cap 8192) with 249,861 RPC submits (2.3x normal), 13,140 gossipsub publish failures and 1,411 AllQueuesFull; val2 received 99,237 vs val1 134,088. Under an ingest burst the pre-spread silently degrades and only the ingest node can include the dropped actions when it leads; there is no alarm on native_gossip_dropped_full. Valid cells show 0 drops.

Watch item: TORUS_VERIFIED_SENDER_CACHE_CAP=32000 covers ~87 s of ingest at 369 actions/s; peak exec queue depth was 44 blocks (~40 s of lag). Exec misses are ~0 today, but if ingest rises or exec lag grows past ~87 s, every miss is a 2 ms recover on the exec thread; size the cap as 2 x nonce window x ingest rate.

The HotStuff thread's futex time is therefore NOT RocksDB write-queue waiting — evidence against the write-queue branch of s64 item 9, and the 'consensus KV split instance' (§3) is unlikely to help.
5. flush_da_mirrors on the HotStuff thread (before selection and before every DA read) is small: the 50 ms age trigger is evaluated on each ingress push (~400/s), so pending is typically 0-20 bodies (<0.4 MB) -> ~0.5-2 ms per call, 2-3 calls per view. Not a blocked-time cause. Minor wart: the age trigger only fires on the next push, so a burst-then-pause leaves bodies buffered until the next selection.
6. Exec does NOT re-check the 60 s nonce window (no NONCE_WINDOW_MS use in native_executor.rs; replay_guard is uniqueness only), so actions selected near expiry are not rejected at exec — rules out 'dead-on-arrival block space' as a loss mechanism.
7. Follower trust-cache pre-check is 100% miss for first-sight gossip (val1 misses 121,367 = received 121,366) and the key is then recomputed at insert (lib.rs 441 and 588); idea 2 folds both into one pass.
8. Pool structures themselves (BTreeMap selection order, expiry BTreeSet, hash_index, seen) are not a cost: pool peaks at ~13.2k entries, inserts/removals are microseconds, evict_expired removes ~130 entries per leader view, selection clones 200 POD PlaceOrderParams batches (~4 MB memcpy, ~1-2 ms). An Arc-shared entry to kill the selection clone would save only ~1-2 ms/view (<0.3%) — not worth an idea. The 30 ms remove_committed cost is entirely the restash key recompute (s64 item 4) and it also holds the pool read lock, stalling all 9 gossip-verify + RPC writers for 30 ms per commit (~3% ingress dead time) — item 4 fixes that too.
9. Lazy/deferred follower verification (verify only what is selected/executed instead of all 121k gossiped actions) would cut ~0.7 core fleet but moves ~45k verifies per follower onto the exec-side verify phase (+~30 ms/block on the exec critical path in the exec-bound late window); not recommended without a pipelined pre-exec verify stage (L effort). Trusted admission from validator peers has the same problem plus pool-pollution risk; skipped.

ideas.title: Lazy deletion in level queues: cancel becomes O(targets) instead of O(depth) memmove/swap
ideas.area: torus-core order_book.rs + order_book/cancel_batch.rs (cancel_all, cancel_all_many, cancel_order, modify_order)
ideas.what_needs_to_be_done: 1) Store `seq` inside `Order` as an in-memory field (the Borsh impl at order_book.rs:2245-2290 is field-explicit, so row/level bytes stay frozen). 2) Mark a cancelled resting order as a tombstone in place instead of removing it from the VecDeque: `remaining_qty = ZERO` is a safe sentinel (place_order rejects qty < lot_size at :377, in-place modify requires new_q > 0 at :719, a full fill pops the entry at :1129-1136), plus a per-level live count (e.g. wrap the queue in `struct Level { q: VecDeque<Order>, live: u32 }`). Drop the level from the BTreeMap when live hits 0. 3) Make every reader skip tombstones: execute_match/match_at_level front (pop and continue), best_bid/best_ask, bid_depth/ask_depth, can_fill_completely, orders_for_trader, verify_invariants, bid_queues/ask_queues (used by save/load), level_row_data/absorb_level, rebuild_all_chunks/rebuild_one_chunk/chunked_top (count and total_qty from live entries only), the whole-book Borsh walk at :2500-2545. queue_position/partition_point keep working because tombstones keep their seq (now read from Order, not from order_seq). 4) Purge: tombstones at the front are consumed by matching for free; run one O(depth) `retain` on a level only when tombstones exceed live/2 (amortized ≤2 moves per element lifetime). 5) Delete cancel_batch.rs (964 lines) and the single-cancel `queue.remove(pos)` at :609 and :670. Validate with the existing differential tests (cancel_batch tests vs the frozen loop; pinned level preimages at :4225-4447; queue_lookup_tests) and a 3+3 interleaved A/B watching phase1_actions ms/blk early vs late.
ideas.reasoning: Phase 1 of execute_batch is almost entirely CancelAllOrders (run-cell.sh:495 `--cancel-fraction 0.05`; 193.6 actions/blk → ~9.7 cancel-alls per block, each all-markets → ~97 book cancel calls per block, ~6.1k target orders per block = 9.7 senders × 63 orders (3.15M resting / 5000 senders / 10 markets) × 10 markets). exec_cancel_all_run → cancel_all_many → apply_cancel_all_many → remove_targets (cancel_batch.rs:104-136, :412-428): the Compact arm swaps every survivor outside the single largest target-free gap, the Reverse/Forward arms call VecDeque::remove. With ~120 targets spread uniformly over an 88k-deep level, the largest gap is a few thousand, so ~85k survivors are swapped: 85k × 3 copies × ~160 B ≈ 40 MB of memory traffic per deep level, 2-4 deep levels per market, 10 markets, serial on the exec thread → ~0.8-1.6 GB moved per block ≈ 100+ ms. That matches the measured late-window phase1 of 113-122 ms and its ~4x growth from the early window (26-33 ms at ~0.9M resting): it is the only engine term that scales with depth (match +20%, margin +15%, settle +28% over the same interval). Lazy deletion makes a cancel O(log depth) probe + ~5 map/journal ops ≈ 2 µs: 6.1k × 2 µs ≈ 12 ms per block plus ~2 MB/blk of amortized purge traffic. Arithmetic: late-window engine 485 → ~380 ms, block 739 → ~635 ms (−14%); 300 s average chain ~700 → ~605 ms (−13%). The last ~120 s of each cell are exec-bound, so with the s64 0.6x dilution: +6-9% matched/s standalone. If s64 item 7 (parallel cancel-all across markets, 111 → 18-37 ms wall) lands first, the wall increment is −10-25 ms (+1-2.5%), but item 7 keeps the ~1 GB/blk of memory traffic spread over 10 threads: ~1 core-second per block per validator, ~3.3 cores of the 18 on a host already at load1 31.6, which this removes.

ideas.what_needs_to_be_done: 1) Add `seq: u64` to `Order` as an in-memory field (custom Borsh impl at :2245-2290 leaves the frozen row bytes unchanged; set it in insert_order/insert_loaded_order, keep it on in-place modify, reassign on cancel+reinsert). With 1024-seq chunks (~256 members): top ≈ 14-18 KB (~0.07 ms); dirty chunks ≈ 4-5 tail + ~11 front per level × ~140 µs (31 KB keccak) ≈ 2.2 ms/level. Net ≈ −1.4 ms per deep level → −6-8 ms wall per block (~1% of chain) and −60 ms CPU/blk. raw.notes: Scope finding for this angle: the per-order and per-fill risk state I/O that used to dominate (S372/S395 memories: margin 13 us/order, settle 78%) is already solved by the per-batch write-back BalanceCache (O1) and PositionCache (C1): Phase 2 is 30 ms/blk for 72.8k orders (0.41 us/order), and cache_flush is 5.5 ms/blk for only 492 dirty balances + 2,796 dirty positions per block (torus_exec_dirty_entries_* / 367). A cross-block resident balance/position cache would therefore save at most ~3.3k overlay get+put per block (~10-15 ms, mostly in parallel pass A) and is not worth its coherence risk; I did not propose it. All four ideas above are small (each <=3% of the 717 ms exec block); I found no 10%-class lever in the margin/economics path. Nothing in torus-economics (staking/rewards/epoch) runs per order or per fill; MarginEngine::check_initial_margin / cross_margin_equity are reached only from liquidation.rs and tests, and liquidation has no production caller in exec_pipeline/committer/app.rs, so there is no per-block risk scan to cache. Workload-realism caveat that changes what these numbers mean: the econ shape sizes every order at qty = 1500*20/30000 = 1.0 -> clamped to ONE lot (bench-throughput main.rs:605-608), and each market's senders are fixed buyers or sellers (:574), so every fill fully consumes exactly one maker, no maker is left partially filled, positions only ever increase, and no realized PnL is ever credited (torus_orders_self_trade_cancels_total 0, orders_rejected_margin 0). Production traffic with partial fills, closes and flips will pay the fill_transition division and the pass-B PnL balance credits per fill, which the bench never exercises. Possible attribution gap: settle pass A wall (90.8 ms/blk) is ~5x my static CPU estimate for one 5.8k-fill market (~15-20 ms), and pidstat shows the process at 423% CPU with only ~305% in named threads, i.e. ~1.2 cores across the 3 nodes in short-lived scoped workers that the 1 Hz sampler cannot attribute; a CLOCK_THREAD_CPUTIME_ID timer per pass-A/match worker would tell preemption from CPU and sharpens s64 item 9. Evidence relevant to an existing estimate: positions are ~95% of the native-root dirty entries (2,796 positions vs 492 balances and 146 book entries per block) while torus_exec_root_seconds is 44.66 s/367 = 122 ms/blk on the flush worker; the s64 trie items (RAM internal nodes, lagged root) and the s450 memories cover this, so I did not list it, but any position-row bucketing change should be evaluated against that 122 ms. Correction to the design-parallel-engine.md section 7 verdict: it remains the only measurement of TORUS_PARALLEL_ENGINE and memory 92541a7 records that its baseline was confounded by direct RocksDB writes.
